sections.label: CDA co-matching and Baby Support Grant
sections.summary: Government doubled CDA co-matching for second child from 1 January 2021 and gave a one-off $3,000 Baby Support Grant for births from 1 October 2020 to 30 September 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: The maximum dollar-for-dollar Government co-matching of parents' savings in the CDA for the second child born from 1 January 2021 was doubled earlier this year, from $3,000 to $6,000.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: To reassure couples to proceed with their parenthood plans despite the global pandemic, the Government also implemented the one-off Baby Support Grant of $3,000 for Singaporean children born from 1 October 2020 to 30 September 2022.

sections.label: Government-Paid Paternity and Adoption Benefits
sections.summary: Clauses 13 and 26 legislate the GPPB and GPAB schemes, with fathers eligible if the child's date of birth or estimated delivery is on or after 1 January 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: Clauses 13 and 26, therefore, legislate the new Government-Paid Paternity Benefit and Government-Paid Adoption Benefit schemes, or GPPB and GPAB respectively, under which such parents can qualify.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: A father can be eligible for GPPB if his child's date of birth or estimated date of delivery is on or after 1 January 2021.

sections.label: GPPB and GPAB application date
sections.summary: Eligible parents may apply for the new GPPB and GPAB schemes from 1 December 2021, with around 500 working fathers and adoptive mothers estimated to benefit.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: As further amendments need to be made to subsidiary legislation, eligible parents may apply for the new GPPB and GPAB schemes from 1 December 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: We estimate that around 500 working fathers and adoptive mothers will benefit.

sections.label: Benefit top-up for retrenched parents
sections.summary: Clauses 8(m), 13 and 26 grant a benefit top-up to retrenched parents who did not manage to take their leave.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: Clauses 8(m), 13 and 26 will address this, by granting a benefit top-up to retrenched parents who did not manage to take their leave.

sections.label: Stillborn child leave and benefits
sections.summary: The Bill lets working parents of a stillborn child who would have been a Singapore Citizen qualify for birth-linked Government-Paid Leave and Benefits Schemes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: The proposed Bill will allow working parents of a stillborn child, who would have been a Singapore Citizen, to qualify for birth-linked Government-Paid Leave and Benefits Schemes – which are maternity leave and benefits, paternity leave and benefits, as well as shared parental leave.

sections.label: Counting stillborn and deceased children
sections.summary: Clause 2(1)(h) counts stillborn or deceased children in determining the number of children a mother has had.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: In addition to the above entitlement to leave and benefits, clause 2(1)(h) will count stillborn children or deceased children in determining the number of children a mother has had.

sections.label: Disqualifying fathers from parental leave
sections.summary: This disqualifies married and unmarried fathers from paid childcare leave and unpaid infant care leave for children born from extramarital affairs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: Five, disqualify wed/unwed fathers from paid childcare leave and unpaid infant care leave, in respect of children born from extramarital affairs.

sections.label: Amendments disqualify fathers from leave
sections.summary: Clauses 18(c), 18(f) and 21(b) disqualify married and unmarried fathers from paid childcare leave and unpaid infant care leave under CDCA for extramarital children.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: With the above in mind, the amendments laid out in clauses 18(c) and (f) and 21(b) disqualify wed and unwed fathers from paid childcare leave and unpaid infant care leave under CDCA with respect to children born from extramarital affairs.

sections.label: Disqualifying mothers from maternity benefit
sections.summary: This disqualifies mothers who have consumed maternity leave under the Employment Act from GPMB.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: Six, disqualify mothers who have consumed maternity leave under the Employment Act (EA) from GPMB.

sections.label: Recovering payments made due to error
sections.summary: The amendment lets the Government recover payments made due to any error, including errors by an electronic system or by any person.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: The amendment will allow the Government to also recover payments that were made due to any error; and this could include, for example, errors caused by an electronic system used by the Government to determine claims or made by any person.

sections.label: Paternity and adoption benefit schemes
sections.summary: This introduces GPPB and GPAB schemes for working fathers and adoptive mothers on short-term contracts or whose contracts expired before birth or adoption, with applications from December 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: So, it will be good if the Government can make exceptions to help them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: It is timely to introduce the Government-Paid Paternity Benefit (GPPB) and the Government Paid Adoption Benefit (GPAB) schemes for working fathers and adoptive mothers who are on short-term employment contracts or whose employment contract had expired before their child was born or adopted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: And adopting children, especially in this challenging climate, is a virtuous act that should receive support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I note that eligible parents can only apply from December 2021.

sections.label: Top-ups for retrenched parents
sections.summary: The Bill proposes GPMB, GPPB or GPAB top-ups for parents who have been retrenched but have unconsumed parental leave.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: (In English): The Bill proposes to grant Government-Paid Maternity Benefit (GPMB), GPPB or GPAB top-ups for parents who have been retrenched but have unconsumed parental leave.

sections.label: Definition of self-employed
sections.summary: A Member asks, on behalf of residents, for clarification of the Bill's definition of self-employed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: On behalf of my residents, I would also like to clarify what is the definition of self-employed in the Bill.

sections.label: Reimbursement for voluntary parental leave
sections.summary: The amendment reimburses employers who voluntarily grant leave to employees not meeting the three-month criterion for parental leave schemes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: With the amendment to this Bill, employers who voluntarily grant leave to their employees who have not met the minimum three-month employment criterion for the various parental leave schemes will also be reimbursed.

sections.label: Government leave benefits and Sweden
sections.summary: The Government can offer any amount of leave benefits, even emulating Sweden's 480 days of paid parental leave.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The Government can offer any amount of leave benefits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: We can even try to emulate Sweden and give parents an entitlement of 480 days of paid parental leave once a child is born or adopted.

sections.label: More grants and loans for pro-family employers
sections.summary: A Member asks if the Government can offer more grants and loans to pro-family employers, similar to subsidies for mature workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Can the Government, perhaps, look into dangling more carrots, including more grants and loans, where pro-family employers can benefit in other areas?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: This could be similar to how the Government provides higher subsidies for hiring of mature workers.

sections.label: Clause 9(a) and stillborn children
sections.summary: Amendments such as clause 9(a) are important because mothers of healthy and stillborn children endure the same physiological trauma.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: That is why amendments, such as that documented in clause 9(a) of the Bill, are so important.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: There is no difference between the physiological trauma endured by the mother of a healthy versus stillborn child.

sections.label: Studies on post-delivery leave periods
sections.summary: Studies suggest 12 weeks post-delivery affects vitality, 15 weeks mental health, and 20 weeks role function.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Studies suggest that a leave period of 12 weeks post-delivery will positively affect vitality, while 15 weeks yield positive effects on mental health and 20 weeks on role function.

sections.label: Marriage age and fertility trends
sections.summary: The median age of female marriages rose to 28.8 years in 2020 while the total fertility rate continues to decline.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Indeed, our latest demographic trends suggest that adoption may become ever-more prevalent, given how the median age of female marriages continues to drift higher – it was 28.8 years in 2020, almost a year more than a decade ago – all while our nation’s total fertility rate continues to decline.

sections.label: Primary caregiver benefit language
sections.summary: The speaker argues benefits should be worded for the primary caregiver so male parents are not excluded by gender.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: If so, fathers might be inadvertently excluded by the benefits outlined in section 12A.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: It strikes me as far more reasonable to couch the language in terms of the primary caregiver, whether it be male or female, in order to preclude the possibility that male parents forever find themselves ineligible for benefits, simply by dint of their gender.

sections.label: Pregnant women workplace scrutiny
sections.summary: Outright dismissals on pregnancy grounds are rare, but pregnant women often feel pressure or scrutiny over workplace performance.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: While outright dismissals purely on the grounds of pregnancy alone are exceedingly rare – not least because they would be deemed wrongful – pregnant women, nevertheless, often feel under immense pressure or scrutiny over their workplace performance.

sections.label: CDA returns and parental benefits
sections.summary: CDA returns reach at most 2% yearly, unlike CPF's legislated 2.5% Ordinary Account minimum, and the speaker welcomes new parental benefits.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Yet, a causal inspection of available CDA offered by the major bank reveals that returns amount to only at most 2% a year.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This is notable especially in contrast to risk-free interest on the other major Government savings scheme, CPF, where there is a legislated mandatory minimum of 2.5% on the Ordinary Account, and significantly higher for other accounts.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: One is left to wonder why CDAs do not enjoy the same legislative protections that CPF offers to its members.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The introduction of the Government-Paid Paternity Benefit (GPPB) and Government-Paid Adoption Benefit (GPAB) is particularly welcomed, as is the provision for retrenched parents to benefit from the top-ups for leave during this very difficult period.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I am very heartened by the support for another group of parents – those with stillborn children – who will receive birth-linked leave and benefits during a distressing juncture in their parenting journey.

sections.label: Twins counted as single delivery
sections.summary: MOM currently considers the birth of twins or multiple babies a single delivery.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Currently, the birth of twins or multiple babies is considered a single delivery by MOM.

sections.label: Multiple births and leave duration
sections.summary: Multiple births are 3% to 4% of births over the last decade and parents' leave days can be spread over a longer duration.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Around 3% to 4% of births over the last decade are multiple births and the days of leave taken by the parents can be spread out over a longer duration, to lower the impact at the workplace.

sections.label: Miscarriage leave policy review
sections.summary: Asks whether the Ministry will review leave policies for mothers who miscarry before the 28th week of pregnancy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Will the Ministry consider going further and reviewing its leave policies where a mother miscarries before the 28th week of pregnancy?

sections.label: Miscarriage leave reimbursement, Baby Bonus cash
sections.summary: Asks whether the Ministry will partially reimburse employers giving leave for pre-28th-week miscarriages, and suggests Baby Bonus cash for single unwed parents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Will the Ministry consider taking a first step by providing partial reimbursements to employers who provide leave benefits to parents where a mother miscarries before the 28th week of pregnancy?

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: My second suggestion is on providing the cash component of the Baby Bonus for single unwed parents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I have spoken up about this many times over the years and it is time that we allow single unwed parents to qualify for the cash component of the Baby Bonus.

sections.label: Baby Bonus discrimination against single unwed parents
sections.summary: States millionaires may receive Baby Bonus cash while single unwed parents do not, though many are low-income.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This discrimination may lead to the odd position where millionaires may be getting cash from the Baby Bonus, cash they do not need.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: But single unwed parents do not receive the same benefits, even though they are parents, too and even though many of them are low-income, with those under 35 years old having just a median salary of $600.

sections.label: NUS paternity leave research findings
sections.summary: Cites NUS research finding paternity leave positively related to family dynamics and children's well-being, with longer leave giving greater benefits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Researchers at NUS looked into this and published their findings just a few months ago: "This is the first evidence-based research that documents the positive relationship between paternity leave provision and family dynamics and children's well-being in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It is useful to see that, in addition to the immediate benefit for fathers to share the joy and responsibility of childcare when a child is born, leave-taking has a mid-to-long-term impact on children's and family's well-being and that a longer leave has greater benefits to the children's well-being." They concluded that a two-week or longer paternity leave is significantly related to lower family conflict, maternal depression and mothers' parenting aggravation, and positively related to marital satisfaction and father-child closeness.

sections.label: IPS paternity leave recommendations
sections.summary: Supports IPS recommendations to extend paternity leave and make it exclusive and non-transferable, targeting equal paternity and maternity leave by 2030 or 2040.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The policy recommendations put forth by the IPS study include extending the length of paternity leave and that, instead of shared parenting leave, exclusive and non-transferable paternity leave can be put in place for parents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I wholeheartedly support this call and hope that we set a target year, perhaps 2030 or 2040, at which we will have an equal number of paternity leave and maternity leave.

sections.label: Reasons public consultation not done
sections.summary: Asks the Minister of State to share reasons why public consultation was not done, if it was not.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: If public consultation was not done, can Minister of State share the reasons why it was not done?

sections.label: Reimbursement for voluntary maternity leave
sections.summary: The Ministry will reimburse companies that voluntarily offer maternity and adoption leave to local female employees with under three months' service.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Under the amendments, the Ministry will now reimburse companies which voluntarily offer maternity and adoption leave to local female employees who have worked for less than three months despite not being required to do so.

sections.label: Single mothers excluded from benefits
sections.summary: Single mothers are left out of the Baby Bonus scheme and are ineligible for parenthood tax rebates and reliefs such as the Working Mothers Child Relief.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: As Member Louis Ng has pointed out, they are left out of the Baby Bonus scheme which provides a cash entitlement of $8,000 for the first and second child.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Furthermore, although many single mothers are in the workforce, they are ineligible for parenthood tax rebates and reliefs, such as the Working Mothers Child Relief (WMCR).

sections.label: Doubled CDA co-matching
sections.summary: The Government recently doubled the maximum dollar-for-dollar co-matching for parents' savings for the Child Development Account for their second child, from $3,000 to $6,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The Government recently doubled the maximum amount of dollar-for-dollar co-matching for parents' savings for the Child Development Account (CDA) for their second child, from $3,000 to $6,000.

sections.label: Benefits for contract workers, still-born children
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes benefit schemes for contract workers, expansion of benefits to parents of still-born children, and extension of the Government-Paid Maternity Benefit to fathers and adoptive mothers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Particularly, we welcome the introduction of benefit schemes for contract workers and the sensible expansion of benefits even to parents of still-born children.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: We cannot tell baby to wait for her parents' economic conditions to make a turn for the better, or for mom and dad to be placed with a permanent job.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: That is why we are encouraged by the Government's consideration of parents on short-term contracts, as seen in the Government-Paid Maternity Benefit and, so, we celebrate its extension to fathers and adoptive mothers as well.

sections.label: Shared parenthood and paternity leave take-up
sections.summary: When both parents are involved they share parenthood responsibilities and joy, and this invitation rides on low paternity leave take-up rates, especially in the private sector.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: However, when both parents are well involved, both share the responsibilities of parenthood and, together with the shared responsibilities, come joy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: This invitation rides on the low take-up rates of paternity leave, especially in the private sector.

sections.label: Incentivising employers for equal parenting
sections.summary: The speaker calls on the Government to incentivise employers to be champions of equal parenting roles, strong families and children.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: But to break out of old mindsets, new approaches must be embraced.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Therefore, we call on the Government to incentivise employers on this front to be champions of equal parenting roles and, so, champions of strong families and children.

sections.label: Equal benefits for single mothers
sections.summary: The Labour Movement's 2013 call led to unwed mothers receiving the same maternity, childcare, infant care leave and CDCA benefits.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In 2013, the Labour Movement had called for equal benefits for single mothers and, as a result, we now see unwed mothers entitled to the same maternity leave, childcare and infant care leave, as well as the enjoyment of CDCA benefits.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: We will continue to stand with single mothers and not compound the burden of having to raise a child singlehandedly.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: These make up just two of our 12 robust and highly actionable recommendations.

sections.label: Debating Child Development Co-Savings Bill
sections.summary: The debate should consider not only how Government helps parents but how it helps parents help each other.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: As we gather to debate the Child Development Co-Savings Bill, our considerations must not only be on how the Government can help parents, but how the Government can help parents help each other as well.

sections.label: Fertility rate and dual-income couples
sections.summary: The 2020 total fertility rate was a historical low, and more than half of married couples are dual-income.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Our total fertility rate (TFR) in 2020 was a historical low.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The last decade has seen an increase in the proportion of resident married-couple households with working wives and, as of 2020, more than half of our married couples are dual-income.

sections.label: Paternity and adoption benefit schemes
sections.summary: The Bill introduces Government-Paid Paternity and Adoption Benefit schemes, amends benefits for short-term contracts, retrenchment and stillborn children.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: COVID-19 with home-based learning and work from home, has also brought about new realities, with a marked effect on what the family unit requires of each of its members, fathers included, and also what employers can expect from employees.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I am glad that this Bill introduces the Government-Paid Paternity Benefit (GPPB) and Government-Paid Adoption Benefit (GPAB) schemes – the former giving fathers more benefits, signalling that they are important, too, when it comes to making trade-offs between work and family.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I understand that eligible parents will be able to apply for these schemes from December 2021 and hope that the Government can provide an indicative timeline on the application process, as I am sure many will be interested to know how they can apply and what sort of records will employers and employees be required to keep to prevent disputes down the line, especially for retrenched parents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I am also glad that we are amending the benefits to recognise short-term employment contracts and parents who are, unfortunately, affected by unforeseen circumstances, such as retrenchment, which can cause great uncertainty, as well as extending compassion to parents of stillborn children, allowing them time to recover physically and emotionally.

sections.label: Covering more childcare leave days
sections.summary: Financially covering more days of childcare leave may reduce employers' financial stress, and discouraging paid leave can be costlier.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: For example, financially covering more days of childcare leave may take some financial stress off employers, instead of only covering the last three days.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Encouraging employees to take paid leave may be costly for employers, but discouraging it or setting up unfriendly work practices can be costlier.

sections.label: Zahid & Shah Group supporting fathers
sections.summary: The founder of Zahid & Shah Group encourages paternity leave, flexible work arrangements and time-off for fathers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: For example, the founder of Zahid & Shah Group encourages their employees to take paternity leave, provides flexible work arrangements and gives time-off to fathers who need to help their wives or accompany their elderly parents to vaccination appointments.

sections.label: Women pressured to abandon careers
sections.summary: The passage states that women are pressured by husbands or families to abandon career aspirations, and calls the Bill a step forward reflecting an inclusive, family-friendly policy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: They are pressured by their husbands or families to abandon their career aspirations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This Bill is a step forward that reflects the Government's policy of being inclusive and family-friendly.

sections.label: Savings match for low-income families
sections.summary: The passage welcomes raising the second-child capped amount from $3,000 to $6,000, notes a $335 monthly shortfall for the bottom 20% of households, and suggests a higher savings match ratio for them.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: While I welcome and support the recent revisions to increase the capped amount for the second child from $3,000 to $6,000, low-income families may be left with a further gap to catch up on, compared to other families in terms of child financing.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Based on the latest Household Expenditure Survey, on average, the bottom 20% of households are now spending $2,570 a month while having a monthly income of $2,235, which includes already the regular Government transfers, such as Workfare.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This means that these 20th percentile of families have a shortfall, on average, of $335 each month, leaving them no ability to save.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I suggest we have a differentiated and higher savings match ratio for households that are within the bottom 20th percentile of income in Singapore, to help make the savings matching scheme more equitable.

sections.label: Children born out of wedlock
sections.summary: The passage says the Government's treatment of children born out of wedlock and within marriages should be equalised, and finds the latest amendments continue to disadvantage children of unwed parents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Third, we should equalise the Government's treatment of children born out of wedlock and within marriages.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I am disappointed that the latest amendments continue to disadvantage children born to unwed parents, which is unfortunate and unfair for the child.

sections.label: Benefits for single parents
sections.summary: The passage states the Government should consider extending benefits to single parents, including those who are unwed, separated or divorced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: First, Mr Deputy Speaker, the Government should consider extending the benefits to single parents, including those who are unwed, separated or divorced.

sections.label: Support for single parents and pregnancy loss
sections.summary: The passage hopes the Government accords single-parent families the same benefits as conventional families, and requests support for stillborn children be extended to miscarriage or other pregnancy loss.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I hope that the Government can accord the same benefits eligible to conventional families to the single-parent families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I also wish to request that support for parents with stillborn children be extended to those who have suffered a miscarriage or other pregnancy loss.

sections.label: Fathers taking paternity leave
sections.summary: The passage states that in 2019 only 45% of all fathers took paternity leave, and that amendments to the Government-Paid Paternity Benefit will be welcomed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In 2019, only 45% of all fathers took paternity leave.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: As such, the amendments to the Government-Paid Paternity Benefit (GPPB) will be welcomed.

sections.label: Equalised Government child benefits
sections.summary: Government benefits supporting children's caregiving, growth and development have been equalised over the years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Over the years, all Government benefits that support the caregiving, growth and development of children have been equalised.

sections.label: CDA for single unwed parents
sections.summary: In 2016 the Child Development Account was extended to children of single unwed parents, including the First Step Grant and matched co-savings.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: In 2016, we further extended the Child Development Account (CDA) to children of single unwed parents, which includes the CDA First Step Grant and matched co-savings from the Government.

sections.label: CDA First Step Grant
sections.summary: In 2016 the CDA First Step Grant was introduced as a $3,000 deposit when the CDA is opened, without parents saving first.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: In 2016, we introduced the CDA First Step Grant, which is a $3,000 deposit when CDA is opened, without parents having to save first.

sections.label: CDA top-up for young children
sections.summary: Under the Household Support Package, all Singaporean children aged six and under in 2021 receive a $200 CDA top-up from September this year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: For example, as part of the Household Support Package announced at Budget this year, all Singaporean children aged six and under in 2021 will receive a $200 top-up to their CDA from September this year.

sections.label: Full-day childcare places growth
sections.summary: Full-day places rose from about 120,000 in 2015 to around 190,000 today, on track to exceed 200,000 by 2023.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: To this end, we have significantly increased the number of full-day places, from about 120,000 in 2015 to around 190,000 today, an increase of over 50%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: To answer Mr Yip Hon Weng's query, in spite of the COVID-19 situation, we are on track to grow the number of full-day places to over 200,000 by 2023.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Today, almost 70% of all childcare centres and over 95% of Anchor Operator childcare centres are located in residential estates, as families have, generally, expressed a preference for childcare services close to their homes.

sections.label: Government-paid portion of leave
sections.summary: Eligible applicants are entitled to Government payment for the Government-paid portion of leave, based on lost income capped by legislative limits.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: If eligible, the applicant will be entitled to payment from the Government for the Government-paid portion of leave, based on one's lost income, as capped by the limits set out in legislation.

sections.label: Parent payout based on income
sections.summary: A parent's payment is derived from average income over the 12 months before the child's birth or adoption eligibility date.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: The amount that a parent receives will be derived from the average income earned over the 12 months preceding the child's date of birth or eligibility date for an adopted child.

sections.label: Payout for benefits-eligible parents
sections.summary: Those not qualifying for leave but eligible for benefits schemes receive a Government payout equal to the Government-paid leave portion, pro-rated by economic activity.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: For those who do not qualify for leave but are eligible for the benefits schemes, they will receive a payout from the Government equivalent to the Government-paid portion of leave, pro-rated based on their economic activity in the 12 months preceding the child's date of birth or the eligibility date for an adopted child.

sections.label: Fathers' paternity leave uptake rise
sections.summary: In 2013, 25% of fathers took paternity leave; in 2019, the proportion rose to 55%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: In 2013, only 25% of fathers took up paternity leave.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: In 2019, the proportion has increased to a healthy 55%.

sections.label: Stillborn child leave eligibility
sections.summary: A stillborn child is defined as delivered after the 22nd week of pregnancy, and parents become eligible for birth-linked leave and benefits.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: A stillborn child is now defined to mean a child delivered after the 22nd week of pregnancy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Parents will become eligible for birth-linked leave and benefits if their child is stillborn after the 22nd week of pregnancy.

sections.label: Stillbirth and adoptive fathers' entitlements
sections.summary: Jamus Lim asked whether shared parental leave could extend to fathers who experienced stillbirth; they are entitled to paternity leave and GPPB, and adoptive fathers qualify for the new GPPB scheme.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Assoc Prof Jamus Lim has asked whether shared parental leave could be extended to fathers who have also experienced a stillbirth.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: They will also be entitled to paternity leave and GPPB.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Adoptive fathers will also qualify for the new GPPB scheme.

sections.label: Marriage and family conversations review
sections.summary: Indranee Rajah and the speaker have led conversations since April on marriage and raising families, with other reviews ongoing and CDCA schemes supporting working parents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Members may be aware that, as part of the Emerging Stronger Conversations, Minister Indranee Rajah and myself have been leading a series of conversations since April with individuals to better understand their experiences and thoughts on getting married and raising families.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: This is an iterative process and I am heartened by the many views shared by my colleagues; and there are also other ongoing reviews related to the conversations on Singapore Women's Development that the Government is leading and I look forward to sharing more in due course.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: The schemes under CDCA, be it the various Leave and Benefits schemes, or CDA, are essential in supporting working parents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: A tapestry of measures and policies must be woven to ensure that families in Singapore are well-supported in their children's growth and development.

sections.label: Single unwed parents' median salary
sections.summary: The speaker stresses that their own data shows single unwed parents under 35 have a median salary of $600.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: Again, I want to stress, we need to remember our own data shows that single unwed parents under 35 have a median salary of $600.

sections.label: CDA revised for single unwed parents
sections.summary: The CDA mentioned earlier was revised in 2016 to also take into account single unwed parents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: The CDA that he mentioned earlier was revised in 2016 to also take into account single unwed parents.

sections.label: CDA interest rates and withdrawals
sections.summary: CDA interest rates are determined by banks, and unlike CPF, parents can withdraw CDA money as needed for their children's upbringing.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: As I shared in my reply earlier, the CDA's interest rates are determined by banks, that is number one.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: And number two, different from CPF, for the CDA account, parents can actually withdraw money from it as and when they need it to defray expenses that they need for the upbringing of their children.
